subject: English
description: Common phrasal verbs (give up, look after, put off, run into, etc.) with meanings

questions.stem: The phrasal verb 'GIVE UP' most closely means:

options.option_text: To donate something to charity
To quit, abandon, or stop trying
To raise someone's hopes high
To return something borrowed

questions.explanation: GIVE UP — quit, surrender, stop trying. 'He gave up smoking last year'. Distractor 1 = GIVE AWAY (donate freely). Distractor 3 = BUILD UP (raise hopes). Distractor 4 = GIVE BACK (return).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: The phrasal verb 'LOOK AFTER' most closely means:

options.option_text: To search for something lost
To take care of or be responsible for
To follow closely with the eyes
To resemble in appearance or manner

questions.explanation: LOOK AFTER — take care of. 'She looks after her elderly parents'. Distractor 1 = LOOK FOR. Distractor 3 = LOOK AT. Distractor 4 = TAKE AFTER ('She takes after her mother').
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: The phrasal verb 'PUT OFF' most closely means:

options.option_text: To wear something on the body
To postpone, delay, or defer
To put something away in storage
To remove an item of clothing

questions.explanation: PUT OFF — postpone. 'The meeting was put off till next week.' Distractor 1 = PUT ON (wear). Distractor 3 = PUT AWAY (store). Distractor 4 = TAKE OFF (remove clothes). 'PUT OFF' can also mean discourage someone ('The smell put me off').
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: The phrasal verb 'RUN INTO' most closely means:

options.option_text: To go very fast in athletics
To meet by chance unexpectedly
To pour liquid into a vessel
To exit a building hurriedly

questions.explanation: RUN INTO — meet by chance. 'I ran into an old friend at the airport.' Also 'encounter unexpectedly' for problems: 'We ran into trouble.' Distractor 1 = RUN FAST. Distractor 3 = POUR INTO. Distractor 4 = RUN OUT (of something).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: The phrasal verb 'BREAK DOWN' (machine sense) most closely means:

options.option_text: To divide into smaller pieces
To stop working due to a fault
To enter forcefully without permission
To start running away from danger

questions.explanation: BREAK DOWN (of a machine, vehicle) — stop functioning. 'My car broke down on the highway.' Of a person — emotional collapse: 'She broke down in tears.' Distractor 1 = BREAK UP (split). Distractor 3 = BREAK IN (forced entry). Distractor 4 = BREAK AWAY (escape).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: The phrasal verb 'CALL OFF' most closely means:

options.option_text: To telephone someone in another city
To cancel a planned event or activity
To shout instructions from a distance
To remove something from the wall

questions.explanation: CALL OFF — cancel. 'The match was called off due to rain.' Distractor 1 = MAKE A CALL. Distractor 3 = CALL OUT (shout). Distractor 4 = unrelated.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: The phrasal verb 'FIGURE OUT' most closely means:

options.option_text: To make a list of all options
To understand or solve by thinking
To draw a chart on the board
To count the number in a group

questions.explanation: FIGURE OUT — understand, solve, work out. 'I can't figure out how this works.' Distractor 1 = LIST OUT. Distractor 3 = DRAW. Distractor 4 = COUNT. Other phrasal verbs of meaning 'understand': make out, work out, fathom out.
